title: End-to-end calibration and schema robustness test for FP8/INT8 serving
creator: Anika Shah
description:
Background: As we convert runtime inference paths to lower-precision formats (FP8 and INT8) to reduce token cost and increase throughput, we observed subtle regressions in structured output produced by function-calling style prompts. This ticket scopes an end-to-end calibration and validation workflow to quantify schema-adherence regressions and propose automated mitigations for production rollouts.

Goal: Produce reproducible calibration pipelines and acceptance criteria that ensure structured/function-call accuracy remains within tolerable limits compared to FP16 baselines. Deliverables: calibration scripts, evaluation harness, per-model calibration artifacts, dashboard (console) smoke checks, rollout policy definitions, and an RFC for fallback behavior when schema adherence drops.

Scope: - Calibration experiments for both FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles across three representative model families used in platform (redwood-small, redwood-base, open-llama-13b). - Offline representative prompt corpus (10k prompts) that exercises function-calling patterns, nested JSON outputs, optional fields, and edge-case value types. - Metrics: schema-validity rate (JSON.parse + JSON Schema), function-call success rate, field-level precision recall for numeric fields, and token-level edit distance for serialized JSON bodies. - Tuning knobs: per-channel vs per-tensor scale, bias-correction, activation clipping schedules, reconstruction datasets, and optional small-weight fine-tune (if needed).

Success criteria (high level): - No more than 0.5% absolute drop in schema-validity rate versus FP16 baseline for hosted API paths under steady-state traffic in canary. - If drop > 0.5% but <= 2.0%, require canary gating plus automatic fallback to FP16 for failing routes. - Any drop > 2.0% is a hard block for turning on the quantized profile for that model in production routes until fixed.

Operational constraints: Calibration must run on dedicated calibration pools, not on production serving GPUs. Artifacts must be versioned and pinned to model+quant-profile. The evaluation harness should be runnable in CI and produce a JSON summary that maps to Console monitors for automated alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration scripts that produce per-layer scale/bias artifacts for FP8 and INT8 and are checked into runtime/calibration/
Evaluation harness that runs schema-adherence tests against a 10k representative prompt set and emits a summary JSON compatible with Console ingestion
Baseline FP16 run recorded and stored as runtime/eval/baselines/<model>-fp16.json for comparison
Canary runbook: 5% traffic canary, 15 minute rolling window eval, automated rollback if schema-validity drops > 0.5% below FP16 baseline
Dashboard panels and automated alerts created: schema-validity, function-call failures, per-field error rates
RFC submitted describing fallback options (route-level FP16, model-variant fallback, and token-level delayed-response fallback)
steps_to_reproduce: Checkout runtime repo and switch to branch quantization/eval/ENG-9016
Upload artifacts to s3://redwood-calibration/<run-id> and run experiments/run_eval.py --model redwood-base --run-id <run-id> --compare-to baselines/redwood-base-fp16.json
Inspect evaluation output at http://console.internal/dashboards/quantization/ENG-9016 or open the JSON summary artifacts
Trigger canary via infra playbook: infra/rollouts/canary-quant-profile.yaml with 5% traffic allocation
comments: 2026-03-10 Anika Shah: Spike identified schema-validity as a fragile metric under naive INT8 conversion for nested JSON outputs; created this ticket to formalize calibration+validation flow.

2026-03-11 Diego Morales: Implemented initial calibration script (scripts/calibrate.py). Ran redwood-base/int8 on representative corpus; initial schema-validity dropped from 99.7% (FP16) to 96.9%—investigating per-layer activation distributions.

2026-03-12 Diego Morales: Tried per-channel scales + bias correction. Schema-validity improved to 98.8% for redwood-base/int8. Noted pattern: failures concentrated in numeric serialization (floats -> truncated strings) and missing optional keys when sampling temperature>0.6.

2026-03-13 Research note: Added numeric-field normalization and stricter sampling constraints in eval harness; rerun shows schema-validity 99.4% for redwood-base/FP8 (with revised activation clipping). Initial open-llama-13b results still show larger delta (FP16 99.3% -> INT8 97.1%).

2026-03-14 Diego Morales: Prepared a canary plan. Pending: add Console panels + create automated alert that maps the evaluation summary metric to severity 'P1' for production routes. Blocking: infra ticket ENG-8921 to expose canary weight toggles for quant profiles.
notes: Decision: start with conservative canaries (5%) and strict schema-validity threshold; relax only after manual review.
Follow-up: if open-llama-13b remains >1.5% drop after calibration knobs, schedule small weight-only quant-aware fine-tune on a 250M token subset (requires infra budget approval).
Experiment idea: compare token-level KL vs schema-validity to see if common token divergence correlates with structural errors.
Cross-team ask: Product should identify customer routes with high structured-output reliance so we can prioritize model profiles for earlier rollouts.
